full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury J: This petition for leave to appeal filed by pre-emptor-petitioner is against judgment of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 331 of 1986 affirming the judgment and order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Rajbari, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 115 of 1985, setting aside the order No. 61 dated 17-7-1985 passed by munsif (now Assistant Judge) Rajbari in Miscellaneous Case No. 76 of 1985 dismissing the application for pre-emption under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 filed by pre-emptor respondent. 

 4. The High Court Division further held on the question of limitation relying on the case of Abdur Rahman vs Baser Ali and others reported in 21 DLR 599 held that the right of pre-emption accrues not on the date of execution but on the date of registration of the document. In the instant case the sale deed was registered under Registration Act on 20-9-78 and pre-emption case was filed on 3-1-1979 i.e. within 4 months from the date of registration of the transfer under section 60 of the Registration Act and therefore the transfer challenged was within time. The High Court Division also held that even if the case land is a homestead or part of it is a homestead it is not exempted from the operation of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and it has not barred pre-emption if the case land is beyond the municipal area. Therefore, the finding and decision of the appellate Court that the pre-emption could be allowed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act in the alternative prayer was redundant. Although part of the case land was part of the agricultural land it is subject to the pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
